dedupe_keys.name: correlation grouping evolutionary algorithm for base station placement in large lte heterogeneous networks

description: This PLOS ONE article proposes an algorithm for placing base stations in large-scale LTE heterogeneous networks, where small cells complement macro cells to serve exponentially growing data traffic but unplanned massive deployment can cause harmful interference. Because evolutionary algorithms are popular global optimisers for radio network planning but degrade as the search space grows, the authors decompose the problem and propose a correlation grouping approach that groups cells according to their mutual interference. Simulation and analytical results indicate that the approach outperforms a random-grouping evolutionary algorithm and an algorithm that detects interacting variables by monitoring changes in the objective function, in terms of system throughput. Producer: the article's authors, published in PLOS ONE in 2015 with a correction dated 12 November 2015. Coverage: generic networks, evaluated in simulation. Access: open access article. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY (PLOS ONE article; version not stated on the page), no code link seen on the page. Caveats: an academic algorithm evaluated on simulated LTE scenarios, with no released implementation confirmed. Simulation uses: it supports optimisation of cell site placement and capacity planning in dense radio networks. Related record: cellular sites and cloudlet placement data for Darmstadt (data-darmstadt-cellular-sites-cloudlet-placement) as an example input.
